NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). Only layer to catch it.</li> <li><strong>Refuter tier:</strong> narrowed 2 blockers via CONTRADICTORY paired verdicts — P2-041 B1 (contract refuter confirmed, reachability refuter refuted the broad form → landed as the narrowed shared fail-closed cooldown verifier, <code>f2c4701</code>) and P2-037 F1 (design vs repro refuters split the same way → F1 narrowed before the fix round). The disagreement itself was the signal; neither single refuter would have produced the narrowed form.</li> <li><strong>Delta re-audits:</strong> 2 fresh blockers in paths newly reachable only after the fix round (P2-037 delta re-audit: blocker=2/should-fix=3), plus the recurring symlink pattern — cooldown provenance <code>Path.resolve</code> unwrapped against symlink loop/OSError, wrapped fail-closed with a cross-version regression test (<code>5f1f161</code>). Neither finding existed in the pre-fix tree; the re-audit layer is what sees post-fix reachability.</li> <li><strong>Lead gates:</strong> P2-044 F1 cadence arithmetic verified directly (all-intervals population; binding Qwen-r3 values asserted exactly: median 0.1199250625, ratio 1.0581313969 — <code>dc1ab95</code>); live NV-5 localhost gate 3/3 OK closing the open lead gate on #49 (<code>10e0ad2</code>); live doctor run. All three are lead-live-only — no static layer could produce them.</li> <li><strong>Integration tree:</strong> 38 pre-merge cross-stream test failures caught at the combined head, dominated by REPRO-002&#39;s fail-closed environment/inventory checks meeting post-cut fields from sibling streams. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Anything user-facing (push/merge/publish) follows the user&#39;s standing instructions.</p> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Date</th> <th>Topic</th> <th>Outcome</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>C-001</td> <td>2026-07-06</td> <td>Adopt review/counterreview between Claude and Codex (2H precedent)</td> <td>adopted; scope enforcement caught the lead&#39;s own stray file (adjudicated benign); floors: request 0.527/0.052 J, phase 1.477/0.786 J, ABBA comparative w/ flagged tail drift; exploratory gross suite: OLMoE ~229 J vs Qwen3-4B ~362.8 J vs 122B ~1072 J (exploratory-labeled) | | C-036 | 2026-07-16 | Resumption + no-hardware batch (Ed: audits in a workflow + &quot;handle the merge yourself if all is well... get the project ready for my quiet mac&quot;; full record <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-16-resumption-nohw-batch.md</code>, the ONE home): ultracode readiness workflow (4 Sol-high audits + severity-tiered refuters) BEFORE work selection; then 4 streams (SPLIT-AP xhigh contract tier, SITE-02 high standard, AXI-SB xhigh spike, AXI-SD Fable web-verification); every fix round delta-re-audited; three self-merges under Ed&#39;s in-session delegation, each with the full D-031-amended gate | PRs #67 (<code>7593259</code>, AXI-SA + CI portability fix after the audit caught red CI), #68 (<code>2778ed2</code>, SITE-02 — D2 step verified EXECUTED in the CI log), #69 (<code>9db4546</code>, SPLIT-AP freeze) merged; integration review 0 cross-stream defects, merged main 1630 OK; kernel closures 51→48 IDs; AXI-SB live probes (lead-run, B∈{2,4}) → verdict <code>supported</code>, Mac C5-2.2 leg mint staged on <code>impl/axi-sb</code> (effective on its merge); delta re-audit caught a LEAD-pinned predictor defect (8th fix-rounds-inject-defects datum, first lead-authored); AXI-SD memo: OLMo pair d_active 0.0016 + 8GB-fit may moot Option A&#39;s premise, Qwen3 pair confirmed-fails G10 (17.17 GB) |</p> <hr> <h2 id="full-entry">Full entry</h2> <h2>C-028: C-027 adjudication and integration arc — infrastructure wave, PRs #49/#54/#55, and the integration window (2026-07-10/11)</h2> <p>Full record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code>; binding rulings: <code>docs/specs/c027/ADJUDICATION.md</code>. No tracked <code>docs/process_traces/</code> artifact is present in this checkout; the run report&#39;s aggregate invocation record is therefore the durable evidence available for this arc, and D-064 governs future tracked event streams. This limitation is recorded rather than repaired with an invented pointer. The arc&#39;s earlier segment (adjudication rounds, PRs #41–#48) is recorded in the CP-5/checkpoint records and stop-card history; this entry records the 2026-07-10/11 continuation.</p> <p>Participants: Fable lead; gpt-5.6-sol as implementer, reviewer, refuter, auditor, and design consultant across ~57 recorded invocations. The lead retained worktree/merge authority, every final diff gate, all live verification, and bookkeeping.</p> <p>Scope of this segment: PR #49 (NV-GATE-2 code-now + flake root-causes) merged <code>1b0f1f6</code> + <code>10e0ad2</code>; PR #54 (P2-041 vetted rebuild from the RED-tranche triage recipe, review + fix round + delta review) merged <code>69a3393</code>; PR #55 (P2-044 idle dependence / HAC / ESS, design-consult-first, review + fix round) merged <code>56d103e</code>. At the Ed-directed pause (stop card checkpoint #4 + amendments) PRs #50–#53 and #56–#58 stood open and lead-gated with the resume order pinned; after resume, the integration tree (<code>c028-integration</code> @ <code>190a0fc</code>, main post-#55 + 7 branches) caught 38 cross-stream failures, the fix round + cross-stream review cleared them, and the full wave merged SHA-guarded (#50, #51, #52, #53, #56, #57, #58 — P2-037 last), with final main verified green and content-identical to the reviewed tree; follow-up PR #59 (from the cross-stream review) is under review and DOC-008 rounds remain in flight. Delegation infrastructure landed on main: adapter, codex-run-v3, usage guard, scope backstop.</p> <p>Closeout amendment (2026-07-11): C-028 is <strong>CLOSED</strong>. PRs #41-#58 are merged; current main&#39;s canonical suite is 1,220 OK (<code>skipped=10</code>) and the corpus gate is 6/6. PR #59 remains open with a 1,224-test green worktree replay (<code>skipped=12</code>), and <code>impl/doc008-kernel</code> is pushed awaiting PR. These open follow-ups do not reopen the card. Every Window-A software gate and P0-003 are satisfied; quiet-machine execution with Ed remains deliberately separate from landed-software status. NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). Only layer to catch it.</li> <li><strong>Refuter tier:</strong> narrowed 2 blockers via CONTRADICTORY paired verdicts — P2-041 B1 (contract refuter confirmed, reachability refuter refuted the broad form → landed as the narrowed shared fail-closed cooldown verifier, <code>f2c4701</code>) and P2-037 F1 (design vs repro refuters split the same way → F1 narrowed before the fix round). The disagreement itself was the signal; neither single refuter would have produced the narrowed form.</li> <li><strong>Delta re-audits:</strong> 2 fresh blockers in paths newly reachable only after the fix round (P2-037 delta re-audit: blocker=2/should-fix=3), plus the recurring symlink pattern — cooldown provenance <code>Path.resolve</code> unwrapped against symlink loop/OSError, wrapped fail-closed with a cross-version regression test (<code>5f1f161</code>). Neither finding existed in the pre-fix tree; the re-audit layer is what sees post-fix reachability.</li> <li><strong>Lead gates:</strong> P2-044 F1 cadence arithmetic verified directly (all-intervals population; binding Qwen-r3 values asserted exactly: median 0.1199250625, ratio 1.0581313969 — <code>dc1ab95</code>); live NV-5 localhost gate 3/3 OK closing the open lead gate on #49 (<code>10e0ad2</code>); live doctor run. All three are lead-live-only — no static layer could produce them.</li> <li><strong>Integration tree:</strong> 38 pre-merge cross-stream test failures caught at the combined head, dominated by REPRO-002&#39;s fail-closed environment/inventory checks meeting post-cut fields from sibling streams. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-open-explore-advisor.md:657:| A47 | FLOOR-COMMONMODE-01 | P2 Next Slice | READY [AGENT] | Pre-register and evaluate a common-mode anchor estimator for ABBA blocks: sweep one shared fiducial shift across all four members, re-integrate measured curves, and add only genuinely per-bundle components adversarially. | The fiducial term is ~80% of the composed anchor bound (24.9 of ~31.1 ms, verified) and is literally the same artifact for all four members of a block; treating it as four independent adversarial draws is itself an unphysical modelling choice. Evidence: Block-timescale fiducial stationarity registered as a NAMED transfer assumption with its evidence; Estimator pre-registered before it touches claim-bearing data; The identical estimator applied to BOTH the calibration blocks and the consuming science contrast (a floor calibrated with cancellation the consumer does not get would understate false effects); Quantified gain on a5/a10 blocks versus the worst-case-sum default. Authority: [2026-07-25 attribution-limit adjudication (Fable ruling + Sol replay; plan in session scratchpad)](docs/decision_log.md). Acceptance: [FLOOR-COMMONMODE-01 acceptance](docs/process/state_kernel.json). Note: Minted 2026-07-25. Quantified same day on a5 decode ABBA (10 complete blocks): implemented worst-case-sum half-width gives a 6.46 J comparative floor; a common-mode proxy gives 2.13 J, a 3x improvement — material, but still above that cell's 0.60 J point floor, so it does not by itself restore extraction under the current gate. Value is in tightening the labelled floor, not in avoiding the label. Fiducial share of the composed bound measured at 80-87%. |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-open-explore-advisor.md:954:Point repeatability is not the full floor. Each energy value is an interval from the timing calibration in Section 3. The floor computation evaluates the complete point-floor estimator over the joint corners of all member intervals that pass the admission and evidence gates, then takes the largest value. For a null A/B/B/A block, the four signed member intervals are propagated through the contrast together. This corner calculation is deliberately conservative: a systematic boundary-placement error is not independent Gaussian noise, so adding it in root-sum-square form would understate the worst case. The published floor is no smaller than the largest accepted attribution width.

Authority: [2026-07-25 attribution-limit adjudication (Fable ruling + Sol replay; plan in session scratchpad)](docs/decision_log.md). Acceptance: [FLOOR-COMMONMODE-01 acceptance](docs/process/state_kernel.json). Note: Minted 2026-07-25. Quantified same day on a5 decode ABBA (10 complete blocks): implemented worst-case-sum half-width gives a 6.46 J comparative floor; a common-mode proxy gives 2.13 J, a 3x improvement — material, but still above that cell's 0.60 J point floor, so it does not by itself restore extraction under the current gate. Value is in tightening the labelled floor, not in avoiding the label. Fiducial share of the composed bound measured at 80-87%. |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-open-explore-contrarian.md:1301:Point repeatability is not the full floor. Each energy value is an interval from the timing calibration in Section 3. The floor computation evaluates the complete point-floor estimator over the joint corners of all member intervals that pass the admission and evidence gates, then takes the largest value. For a null A/B/B/A block, the four signed member intervals are propagated through the contrast together. This corner calculation is deliberately conservative: a systematic boundary-placement error is not independent Gaussian noise, so adding it in root-sum-square form would understate the worst case. The published floor is no smaller than the largest accepted attribution width.

# U5–U7 executable implementation plan

This plan uses the landed U1/U3/U4 behavior, not the older numeric or structural assumptions in the design memo.

Branch heads verified:

- U1: `1cf7a42048a5bfe3841b699c430bf6ebc7cd0664`
- U3: `454f77795f5ed2f1841055a7ce125e1456f583de`
- U4: `35ba641f049b043668b2a45b8005ca94c83b061f`

A sandbox restriction prevented updating `.git/FETCH_HEAD`; the remote branch blobs were independently checked through the connected GitHub repository and matched these local refs. All three are now ancestors of main.

## 1. Landed-branch corrections that bind all three sessions

1. U1 uses five receipts per successful window:

   1. `bracket-session-open`
   2. `bracket-session-slot-claim` for `pre`
   3. `bracket-session-slot-finalization` for `pre`
   4. `bracket-session-slot-claim` for `post`
   5. `bracket-session-slot-finalization` for `post`

   From issuance sequence 76, three uninterrupted successful sessions end at 91, not 85. Individual closeouts would be 81, 86, and 91. Do not put any of these sequence literals into campaign-pack bytes: U8 derives `terminal_sequence = arm_baseline_sequence + 5`.

2. U1 session identity is exactly:

   ```text
   session_id
   window_id
   plan_id
   plan_sha256
   evidence_root_id
   runs_root
   ```

   `runs_root` must be absolute at arm time. `window_id` is frozen equal to `plan_id`.

3. U1 bracket bindings must contain exactly:

   ```text
   schema_version
   ledger_schema
   session_id
   window_id
   plan_id
   plan_sha256
   evidence_root_id
   runs_root
   capability_receipt_digest
   terminal_head
   endpoints
   binding_digest
   ```

   Each `pre`/`post` endpoint carries `attempt_id`, `receipt_digest`, and `content_digest`.

4. U3 requires exactly two producers, and each producer requires exactly two roles whose set is exactly `{decode, prefill}`:

   | Role | Metric | Precheck |
   |---|---|---|
   | `decode` | `phase_energy_j.decode` | `["phase","decode"]` |
   | `prefill` | `phase_energy_j.prefill` | `["phase","prefill"]` |

   Therefore U5 and U6 must not emit separate files falsely claiming to be complete U3 `pinRequirements`. Each emits a producer contract; U8 combines the two contracts, in fixed alpha-then-beta order, with arm-time runtime and acceptance attachments into the single conforming two-producer document.

5. U3’s current order authentication has a landed defect for the required rider shape. It obtains 100 IDs from the four extraction cells, while the executable manifest correctly contains 50 unique runs. Its manifest reader also rejects duplicate run IDs, so a 100-row workaround is impossible.

   U5 must repair `scripts/mint_floor_artifact.py::_validate_order` by comparing the manifest against the stable unique physical union:

   ```python
   physical_spec_ids = list(dict.fromkeys(spec_ids))
   ```

   The manifest must equal and order those 50 IDs. Per-cell duplicate rejection remains in `validate_extraction_spec`; the target-cell subsequence must still equal the target cell’s order. Add a generalized regression proving four cells, 100 references, 50 unique bundles. Preserve all existing v1 behavior.

6. The memo’s common order-manifest field list does not match the landed consumers:

   - `run_campaign.py` consumes `executed_order[].config` and contiguous unique `index`; it optionally propagates row metadata.
   - U3 authenticates the manifest byte SHA, `manifest_id`, `plan_id`, `calibration_plan_sha256`, unique `run_id` membership, and target subsequence.
   - U4 consumes no campaign order manifest.
   - Generator hashes, external references, stage links, evidence roots, attachment slots, and retry policy therefore belong in `plan_tree.json`, not in unsupported root-manifest semantics.

7. U4’s fixture plan IDs are shortened synthetic placeholders. Do not copy them. Use the D-117 identifiers below.

## 2. Frozen cross-pack vocabulary

### Window identities

| Pack | Plan/window ID | Evidence-root ID | Claim-root leaf | Bound-root leaf |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alpha | `plan-d117-floor-qwen25-1p5b-decode-p128-prefill-rider-v1` | `evidence-d117-floor-qwen25-1p5b-v1` | `runs_d117_floor_qwen25_1p5b_v1` | `runs_d117_floor_qwen25_1p5b_v1_bound` |
| Beta | `plan-d117-floor-qwen25-7b-decode-p128-prefill-rider-v1` | `evidence-d117-floor-qwen25-7b-v1` | `runs_d117_floor_qwen25_7b_v1` | `runs_d117_floor_qwen25_7b_v1_bound` |
| Gamma | `plan-d117-contrast-qwen25-1p5b-vs-7b-decode-v1` | `evidence-d117-contrast-qwen25-1p5b-vs-7b-v1` | `runs_d117_contrast_qwen25_1p5b_vs_7b_v1` | `runs_d117_contrast_qwen25_1p5b_vs_7b_v1_bound` |

### Floor artifact vocabulary

```text
plan_set_id:
  plan-set-d117-qwen25-1p5b-7b-phase-floor-v1

aggregate_artifact_id:
  d117-qwen25-phase-floor-set-v1

producer order:
  1. alpha
  2. beta
```

| Producer/role | Artifact cell ID | Transport group ID |
|---|---|---|
| Alpha decode | `d117-qwen25-1p5b-decode-floor-v1` | `tg-d117-qwen25-1p5b-decode-v1` |
| Alpha prefill | `d117-qwen25-1p5b-prefill-p128-floor-v1` | `tg-d117-qwen25-1p5b-prefill-p128-v1` |
| Beta decode | `d117-qwen25-7b-decode-floor-v1` | `tg-d117-qwen25-7b-decode-v1` |
| Beta prefill | `d117-qwen25-7b-prefill-p128-floor-v1` | `tg-d117-qwen25-7b-prefill-p128-v1` |

Component artifact IDs:

```text
d117-qwen25-1p5b-phase-floor-component-v1
d117-qwen25-7b-phase-floor-component-v1
```

Allowed consumer families:

- Alpha decode: only `sw-decode-a-qwen25-1p5b`.
- Beta decode: only `sw-decode-b-qwen25-7b`.
- Alpha prefill: only `df-ph-prefill-p128-qwen25-1p5b`.
- Beta prefill: only `df-ph-prefill-p128-qwen25-7b`.

Aggregate rules:

```text
cell_composition_rule = componentwise_max_never_sum.v1
consumer_floor_rule   = cross_stack_armwise_max.v1
```

## 3. Common generator and plan-tree contract

The existing generators are zero-argument, in-place, and campaign-hardcoded. They cannot be safely parameterized. Each pack gets a new pack-local generator.

Required CLI:

```text
python3 <pack>/generate_configs.py
python3 <pack>/generate_configs.py --check
python3 <pack>/generate_configs.py --output-root <temporary-repo-root>
```

Generation must use explicit filenames formed from fixed numeric ranges. Production code must not use `glob`, `rglob`, `os.walk`, or directory discovery.

Generate in this acyclic order:

1. Read the generator’s own bytes and calculate its SHA.
2. Copy or generate condition-family files.
3. Generate `calibration_plan.json` and its sidecar.
4. Generate science configs with the completed plan SHA.
5. Generate stage manifests.
6. Generate the root order manifest.
7. Generate extraction spec or prospective analysis manifest.
8. Generate the floor producer contract where applicable.
9. Generate `plan_tree.json` last, then its sidecar.

Sidecars use exactly:

```text
<64-lowercase-hex><two spaces><filename>\n
```

### `order_manifest.json`

Keep `schema_version = "joulewise.order_manifest.v1"` and its established top-level shape:

```text
schema_version
manifest_id
plan_id
calibration_plan_sha256
planned_n_bundles
subcampaign_order
executed_order
```

Add `config_sha256` to every stage and root `executed_order` row. Add the stage manifest’s path, ID, and SHA to each root `subcampaign_order` row. The runner may ignore these additions; tests and U8 must enforce them.

Root order manifests contain science only: 50 alpha/beta runs or 40 gamma runs. Operational NEG8, reference, calibration, and closeout stages live in `plan_tree.json`.

### `plan_tree.json`

Every pack emits `schema_version = "joulewise.frozen_plan_tree.v1"` with these exact top-level sections:

```text
schema_version
plan
generator
window_identity
roots
campaign_policy
acceptance_policy
condition_families
science
stage_graph
external_inputs
attempt_policy
arm_attachments
closeout_attachments
downstream_contract
runtime_budget
```

Required contents:

- `plan`: path, plan ID, actual SHA, declared SHA, sidecar path, sidecar SHA.
- `generator`: relative path and byte SHA.
- `window_identity`: `window_id == plan_id`, evidence-root ID.
- `roots`: claim and bound leaf names only. Absolute roots are arm attachments.
- `campaign_policy`: exact path and SHA of `quiet_mac_p2_production.json`.
- `condition_families`: path, byte SHA, family ID, and canonical domain SHA.
- `science`: exact ordered rows containing ordinal, stage ID, config path, config SHA, run ID, role, block ID/index, position, and arm where applicable.
- `stage_graph`: fixed stage IDs, ordinal, kind, expected count, predecessor, successor, and exact manifest/external-input reference.
- `external_inputs`: exact manifest path/SHA plus exact member path/SHA rows—never just a directory.
- `attempt_policy`: zero calibration retries, zero science replacements, no top-ups, failure abort semantics.
- `arm_attachments`: fields unavailable until readiness.
- `closeout_attachments`: binding, terminal head, verdict, basis, and backup requirements.
- `downstream_contract`: extraction/producer contract or prospective analysis path and SHA.
- `runtime_budget`: memo planning estimate, explicitly marked non-authoritative for member replacement.

The final tree is not referenced by any child artifact; this prevents a hash cycle.

Common pinned external inputs:

## 7. U8 readiness-validator contract

U8 must accept an explicit `plan_tree.json` path. It must not locate packs, stages, configs, or attachments by glob.

### Desk phase

For all packs:

- Validate the tree schema and sidecar.
- Run the named generator in `--check` mode.
- Recompute every plan, generator, config, manifest, family, downstream-contract, and external-input SHA.
- Compare the actual filesystem with the explicit inventory.
- Validate all plan/tree/manifest cross-links and IDs.
- Reject duplicate run IDs, paths, cell IDs, transport IDs, or stage ordinals.
- Reject historical evidence roots, receipts, results, operative literals, or evaluation bases.
- Validate zero retries/replacements/top-ups.
- Validate the complete predecessor/successor stage chain.

Alpha/beta additional checks:

- 50 science runs, 12 bound members, 7 references.
- Four extraction cells.
- Exactly 100 cell references and 50 unique bundles/configs.
- Exact `{decode,prefill}` role pair.
- Exact metric/precheck mapping.
- Decode/prefill component membership is identical.
- Four unique artifact cell IDs and four unique transport IDs across the combined alpha/beta contracts.
- Producer and aggregate arrays are positionally alpha-decode, alpha-prefill, beta-decode, beta-prefill.

Gamma additional checks:

- Forty science runs and ten complete blocks.
- No prefill.
- Exact aggregate plan-set/artifact IDs.
- Only alpha/beta decode cells selected.
- `cross_stack_armwise_max.v1`, never sum.

### Pre-arm phase

U8 must require an immutable readiness record supplying:

- Reviewed clean commit and plan-tree SHA.
- Absolute claim and bound roots whose leaf names match the tree and are fresh.
- `waivers.json == []`.
- U1 session ID and distinct pre/post attempt IDs.
- Exact absolute U1 `runs_root`.
- Current committed physical ledger head.
- Current issued acceptance or authenticated U2 descendant.
- U2 registry proof.
- Model artifact SHA and projected runtime-identity SHA.
- Installed runtime/tool/environment identity.
- Offline model availability.
- Zero-agent and quiet-machine gates.
- Campaign policy SHA.
- For gamma, exact validated U10 aggregate artifact SHA.

U8 then composes the single two-producer U3 `pinRequirements` from alpha and beta contracts. It must require exactly two producers and exactly `{decode,prefill}` per producer. A changed acceptance or runtime identity requires new requirement/readiness bytes before member one.

### Post-window phase

Require:

- The exact five-receipt U1 lifecycle.
- Finalized pre/post observations.
- Exact session identity across all receipts.
- Exact bracket binding.
- Terminal physical head equal to committed head.
- Passed whole-window verdict.
- Exact evaluation-basis membership.
- No open/abandoned session or unresolved attachment.
- Two verified backups for evidence and bound roots.

Terminal sequence is always derived from the arm baseline. U4’s 91 remains only the regression oracle for three uninterrupted sessions beginning at 76.

## 8. Fields required by the memo that no template carries

These must be generated or attached as specified above:

- `evidence_root_id`.
- Separate claim/bound root leaves.
- `window_id`.
- Absolute U1 `runs_root`.
- Session, slot, attempt, receipt, binding, and terminal-head identities.
- Generator SHA.
- Config SHAs in order rows.
- Stage predecessor/successor graph.
- Plan-tree digest.
- Zero-calibration-retry and zero-science-replacement policy.
- Prefill-rider mapping over existing physical bundles.
- Prefill family definitions and hashes.
- Artifact cell, transport, component-artifact, aggregate-artifact, and plan-set IDs.
- Transport consumer allowlists.
- Four-cell/100-reference/50-unique extraction relationship.
- U3 `runtime_identity_sha256`, which comes from the authenticated stack identity and cannot be honestly copied from a campaign template.
- Fresh `config_set_sha256`.
- Selected acceptance successor, if any.
- Future verdict, evaluation basis, receipt/content digests, bracket-binding SHA, terminal head, extraction report, and six-decimal operative literals.
- Gamma’s future combined floor-artifact SHA.
- Prospective arm/postcollection attachment slots.

## 9. Execution order

1. Run U5 first. It owns the shared U3 unique-physical-union order repair.
2. Run U6 after U5 lands and passes the full suite.
3. Run U7 after the vocabulary above is fixed; its pack may be built before collection, but gamma cannot arm until U10 supplies the exact combined artifact SHA.
4. U8 consumes the three `plan_tree.json` files and the two producer contracts.
5. Alpha and beta collect and close before U10.
6. U10 mints and validates the four-cell artifact.
7. Gamma readiness binds that exact artifact SHA, then gamma may arm.

## 1. Landed-branch corrections that bind all three sessions

1. U1 uses five receipts per successful window:

   1. `bracket-session-open`
   2. `bracket-session-slot-claim` for `pre`
   3. `bracket-session-slot-finalization` for `pre`
   4. `bracket-session-slot-claim` for `post`
   5. `bracket-session-slot-finalization` for `post`

   From issuance sequence 76, three uninterrupted successful sessions end at 91, not 85. Individual closeouts would be 81, 86, and 91. Do not put any of these sequence literals into campaign-pack bytes: U8 derives `terminal_sequence = arm_baseline_sequence + 5`.

2. U1 session identity is exactly:

   ```text
   session_id
   window_id
   plan_id
   plan_sha256
   evidence_root_id
   runs_root
   ```

   `runs_root` must be absolute at arm time. `window_id` is frozen equal to `plan_id`.

3. U1 bracket bindings must contain exactly:

   ```text
   schema_version
   ledger_schema
   session_id
   window_id
   plan_id
   plan_sha256
   evidence_root_id
   runs_root
   capability_receipt_digest
   terminal_head
   endpoints
   binding_digest
   ```

   Each `pre`/`post` endpoint carries `attempt_id`, `receipt_digest`, and `content_digest`.

4. U3 requires exactly two producers, and each producer requires exactly two roles whose set is exactly `{decode, prefill}`:

   | Role | Metric | Precheck |
   |---|---|---|
   | `decode` | `phase_energy_j.decode` | `["phase","decode"]` |
   | `prefill` | `phase_energy_j.prefill` | `["phase","prefill"]` |

   Therefore U5 and U6 must not emit separate files falsely claiming to be complete U3 `pinRequirements`. Each emits a producer contract; U8 combines the two contracts, in fixed alpha-then-beta order, with arm-time runtime and acceptance attachments into the single conforming two-producer document.

5. U3’s current order authentication has a landed defect for the required rider shape. It obtains 100 IDs from the four extraction cells, while the executable manifest correctly contains 50 unique runs. Its manifest reader also rejects duplicate run IDs, so a 100-row workaround is impossible.

   U5 must repair `scripts/mint_floor_artifact.py::_validate_order` by comparing the manifest against the stable unique physical union:

   ```python
   physical_spec_ids = list(dict.fromkeys(spec_ids))
   ```

   The manifest must equal and order those 50 IDs. Per-cell duplicate rejection remains in `validate_extraction_spec`; the target-cell subsequence must still equal the target cell’s order. Add a generalized regression proving four cells, 100 references, 50 unique bundles. Preserve all existing v1 behavior.

6. The memo’s common order-manifest field list does not match the landed consumers:

   - `run_campaign.py` consumes `executed_order[].config` and contiguous unique `index`; it optionally propagates row metadata.
   - U3 authenticates the manifest byte SHA, `manifest_id`, `plan_id`, `calibration_plan_sha256`, unique `run_id` membership, and target subsequence.
   - U4 consumes no campaign order manifest.
   - Generator hashes, external references, stage links, evidence roots, attachment slots, and retry policy therefore belong in `plan_tree.json`, not in unsupported root-manifest semantics.

7. U4’s fixture plan IDs are shortened synthetic placeholders. Do not copy them. Use the D-117 identifiers below.

## 3. Common generator and plan-tree contract

The existing generators are zero-argument, in-place, and campaign-hardcoded. They cannot be safely parameterized. Each pack gets a new pack-local generator.

Required CLI:

```text
python3 <pack>/generate_configs.py
python3 <pack>/generate_configs.py --check
python3 <pack>/generate_configs.py --output-root <temporary-repo-root>
```

Generation must use explicit filenames formed from fixed numeric ranges. Production code must not use `glob`, `rglob`, `os.walk`, or directory discovery.

Generate in this acyclic order:

1. Read the generator’s own bytes and calculate its SHA.
2. Copy or generate condition-family files.
3. Generate `calibration_plan.json` and its sidecar.
4. Generate science configs with the completed plan SHA.
5. Generate stage manifests.
6. Generate the root order manifest.
7. Generate extraction spec or prospective analysis manifest.
8. Generate the floor producer contract where applicable.
9. Generate `plan_tree.json` last, then its sidecar.

Sidecars use exactly:

```text
<64-lowercase-hex><two spaces><filename>\n
```

### `order_manifest.json`

Keep `schema_version = "joulewise.order_manifest.v1"` and its established top-level shape:

```text
schema_version
manifest_id
plan_id
calibration_plan_sha256
planned_n_bundles
subcampaign_order
executed_order
```

Add `config_sha256` to every stage and root `executed_order` row. Add the stage manifest’s path, ID, and SHA to each root `subcampaign_order` row. The runner may ignore these additions; tests and U8 must enforce them.

Root order manifests contain science only: 50 alpha/beta runs or 40 gamma runs. Operational NEG8, reference, calibration, and closeout stages live in `plan_tree.json`.

### `plan_tree.json`

Every pack emits `schema_version = "joulewise.frozen_plan_tree.v1"` with these exact top-level sections:

```text
schema_version
plan
generator
window_identity
roots
campaign_policy
acceptance_policy
condition_families
science
stage_graph
external_inputs
attempt_policy
arm_attachments
closeout_attachments
downstream_contract
runtime_budget
```

Required contents:

- `plan`: path, plan ID, actual SHA, declared SHA, sidecar path, sidecar SHA.
- `generator`: relative path and byte SHA.
- `window_identity`: `window_id == plan_id`, evidence-root ID.
- `roots`: claim and bound leaf names only. Absolute roots are arm attachments.
- `campaign_policy`: exact path and SHA of `quiet_mac_p2_production.json`.
- `condition_families`: path, byte SHA, family ID, and canonical domain SHA.
- `science`: exact ordered rows containing ordinal, stage ID, config path, config SHA, run ID, role, block ID/index, position, and arm where applicable.
- `stage_graph`: fixed stage IDs, ordinal, kind, expected count, predecessor, successor, and exact manifest/external-input reference.
- `external_inputs`: exact manifest path/SHA plus exact member path/SHA rows—never just a directory.
- `attempt_policy`: zero calibration retries, zero science replacements, no top-ups, failure abort semantics.
- `arm_attachments`: fields unavailable until readiness.
- `closeout_attachments`: binding, terminal head, verdict, basis, and backup requirements.
- `downstream_contract`: extraction/producer contract or prospective analysis path and SHA.
- `runtime_budget`: memo planning estimate, explicitly marked non-authoritative for member replacement.

The final tree is not referenced by any child artifact; this prevents a hash cycle.

Common pinned external inputs:

- Policy SHA: `b0d7b228b88bea717aa9269c103aca760cc36cf05239e0f86c235b4b29665efd`.
- NEG8 manifest SHA: `0ec9d68aa4265cc9378bb682091a973fc92879b76506fa25af828050a608509f`.
- NEG8 corpus SHA: `74ccdaec74497c3aa7c074ef1129ec2bf2cc01d8ac14d3d07be77ab468599688`.
- Start reference manifest: `9cac197255bdc9a0a1a0b8ee8ceb587ba3c8cabc20b976b2543dc3a400d37cb0`.
- Midpoint reference manifest: `9ccedd91307985ba5641e791f4ac89f4e250fca414a4ba713cc7977ced6abb21`.
- End reference manifest: `8e65a4347aafa0722a60a2bd58c7e8061b860db66fa06f6acec24d1a1ade5c67`.
- Issued acceptance:
  - ID `d079_calibration_acceptance_v2_n19`
  - artifact SHA `316113960c596a6f927987dbdf8f2bca4b0cca9ee4a59a540bbd32bba9048985`
  - derivation SHA `4f6633d5fb89a6e8fd137a834728b843915027b6f0b0afd6c37ae24e65d23f02`

## 7. U8 readiness-validator contract

U8 must accept an explicit `plan_tree.json` path. It must not locate packs, stages, configs, or attachments by glob.

### Desk phase

For all packs:

- Validate the tree schema and sidecar.
- Run the named generator in `--check` mode.
- Recompute every plan, generator, config, manifest, family, downstream-contract, and external-input SHA.
- Compare the actual filesystem with the explicit inventory.
- Validate all plan/tree/manifest cross-links and IDs.
- Reject duplicate run IDs, paths, cell IDs, transport IDs, or stage ordinals.
- Reject historical evidence roots, receipts, results, operative literals, or evaluation bases.
- Validate zero retries/replacements/top-ups.
- Validate the complete predecessor/successor stage chain.

Alpha/beta additional checks:

- 50 science runs, 12 bound members, 7 references.
- Four extraction cells.
- Exactly 100 cell references and 50 unique bundles/configs.
- Exact `{decode,prefill}` role pair.
- Exact metric/precheck mapping.
- Decode/prefill component membership is identical.
- Four unique artifact cell IDs and four unique transport IDs across the combined alpha/beta contracts.
- Producer and aggregate arrays are positionally alpha-decode, alpha-prefill, beta-decode, beta-prefill.

Gamma additional checks:

- Forty science runs and ten complete blocks.
- No prefill.
- Exact aggregate plan-set/artifact IDs.
- Only alpha/beta decode cells selected.
- `cross_stack_armwise_max.v1`, never sum.

### Pre-arm phase

U8 must require an immutable readiness record supplying:

- Reviewed clean commit and plan-tree SHA.
- Absolute claim and bound roots whose leaf names match the tree and are fresh.
- `waivers.json == []`.
- U1 session ID and distinct pre/post attempt IDs.
- Exact absolute U1 `runs_root`.
- Current committed physical ledger head.
- Current issued acceptance or authenticated U2 descendant.
- U2 registry proof.
- Model artifact SHA and projected runtime-identity SHA.
- Installed runtime/tool/environment identity.
- Offline model availability.
- Zero-agent and quiet-machine gates.
- Campaign policy SHA.
- For gamma, exact validated U10 aggregate artifact SHA.

U8 then composes the single two-producer U3 `pinRequirements` from alpha and beta contracts. It must require exactly two producers and exactly `{decode,prefill}` per producer. A changed acceptance or runtime identity requires new requirement/readiness bytes before member one.

### Post-window phase

Require:

- The exact five-receipt U1 lifecycle.
- Finalized pre/post observations.
- Exact session identity across all receipts.
- Exact bracket binding.
- Terminal physical head equal to committed head.
- Passed whole-window verdict.
- Exact evaluation-basis membership.
- No open/abandoned session or unresolved attachment.
- Two verified backups for evidence and bound roots.

Terminal sequence is always derived from the arm baseline. U4’s 91 remains only the regression oracle for three uninterrupted sessions beginning at 76.

## 9. Execution order

1. Run U5 first. It owns the shared U3 unique-physical-union order repair.
2. Run U6 after U5 lands and passes the full suite.
3. Run U7 after the vocabulary above is fixed; its pack may be built before collection, but gamma cannot arm until U10 supplies the exact combined artifact SHA.
4. U8 consumes the three `plan_tree.json` files and the two producer contracts.
5. Alpha and beta collect and close before U10.
6. U10 mints and validates the four-cell artifact.
7. Gamma readiness binds that exact artifact SHA, then gamma may arm.
